findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_mak_topic_sources, get_mak_rcic_contact · Private data: get_mak_topic_sources, get_mak_change_ledger, get_mak_rcic_contact · Public sink: get_mak_rcic_contact.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_mak_topic_sources, get_mak_rcic_contact · Private data: get_mak_topic_sources, get_mak_change_ledger, get_mak_rcic_contact · Public sink: get_mak_rcic_contact

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_mak_topic_sources" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Return a curated source set for one of four MAK Canadian immigration education topics: the named licensed MAK expert, a MAK educational resource, the relevant Government of Canada destination, and any already-published independent or owned-media reference included in this source set. This is general" → after: "Use this read-only tool when a user asks for current official-source navigation or verified educational sources about Canadian spousal sponsorship relationship evidence or procedural fairness letters, business immigration source-of-funds or financial evidence, Canadian Experience Class work-experien"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
